_comment: How videos are built. Brand values (palette, fonts, output size and fps) come from config/brand.json and are merged in by video/lib/kitconfig.py; do not copy them here. Every agent and build script reads the merged result. /setup writes the caption choices below from your answers.

output._comment: Width, height and fps come from config/brand.json 'output'. Rule: footage in at the house resolution and fps goes out at the same resolution and fps. Never downscale a master, never change the frame rate mid-pipeline. Verify every render with ffprobe (width, height, r_frame_rate).

caption_playres.note: captions.py authors at this PlayRes; libass scales to the real frame, so caption size/y below are in 1080x1920 space and need no change for 4K.

captions.position_note: y is the vertical centre in a 1080x1920 frame. Lower third (y ~1380) sits over the chest for a head-and-shoulders framing; centre (y 960) suits split-screen podcast shorts. Measure against your own framing: captions must clear the hands, the desk edge and the chin.
captions.outline_note: always = every caption gets an outline (pick this if you film against a light background, so the look is consistent). 'adaptive' = outline only where the background under the caption is light. 'never' = no outline.
captions.highlight_note: Empty = the palette accent. Words in accent_words are drawn in this colour.

grade._comment: HOUSE COLOUR GRADE, applied to every video so all outputs share one look. Empty until the colour-grader agent builds one with you from a still of your footage. Keep it as an ffmpeg filter string plus a note of the intent.
grade.applied_in: Baked into the per-segment vf during the raw-footage cut. For a video that arrives already cut, apply the same filter as a grade pass BEFORE captions and graphics.

graphics.title_note: Big headline/title text uses the title font in the accent colour. In HTML/CSS load fonts with @font-face src: local('<exact face name>') or a base64 data: URI. NEVER url(file://...): it silently falls back to a serif.
graphics.label_weight_note: Labels and eyebrows use the body font at 600/700. Register the real weights with separate @font-face rules: a single Regular @font-face renders thin because font-weight has no real face to use.

animations.energy_note: high = full-screen takeovers, hard snaps, slamming type. punchy = quick, confident, no shake. refined = slow eases, small scale.
animations.never_cut_note: When a finished cut is supplied, it is final. NEVER trim, cut or reorder it. Only add captions and animation overlays.
animations.minimalism_rule: ONE simple primitive per beat: the least graphic that conveys the idea. Allowed primitives: counter, line_graph, pie, bars, arrow, text_slam. Never bespoke many-element compositions (no swarms of dots, no dozens of converging lines). Energy comes from scale and motion, not from adding elements.
animations.text_rule: All on-screen text is crisp and full-opacity once revealed. No faint, low-contrast or pre-appearing labels. Spelling follows config/brand.json locale. Sentence case for sentences; short ALL-CAPS labels are allowed for energy.
animations.medium_note: Engines: Remotion (React, default) or HyperFrames (HTML/CSS via npx hyperframes). For HyperFrames, fonts MUST load with @font-face src: local('<exact face name>') or a base64 data: URI. Caption fontsdir must be a CLEAN font dir (only font files): libass tries to load every file in it and chokes on non-fonts.
animations.constant_motion_note: A graphic is always moving while on screen, OR it completes its motion and then holds still until it leaves. Never start-stop-start. The climax lands the section's key point; the graphic is gone within ~0.5-0.8 s after it lands. Scenes ~2-4 s; face and captions carry the rest.
animations.taste_rule: Subtle, minimal, clear. No checkmarks, clip-art icons, emoji or gimmicks. Convey meaning through the graphic itself (a bar reaching a line = works; an accent-coloured shortfall = fails), never literal symbols.
animations.no_intricate_alignment: If a design needs precise alignment of many small elements (labels under bars, grids, calendars) and there is ANY risk of misalignment, simplify radically or skip. A misaligned graphic is worse than no graphic.
animations.one_beat_one_idea: Never combine two separate sentences or ideas into one graphic.
animations.text_slam_primitive: Full-screen text slams are valid: background colour + a single phrase (accent or text colour), timed to the word. Zero alignment risk, maximum impact for emotional beats.
animations.label_positioning: Place labels OUTSIDE the graphic area (above, below, sides) so lines, bars and arrows cannot reach them.
